answer_1.quote: We train reaction inference models to predict MRF dimensions from headlines. For free-text inferences (e.g. writer intent, reader perception), we use generative language models, specifically T5 encoder-decoder and GPT-2 decoder-only models.
answer_1.outputs: free-text implications for writer intent, reader perception, and reader action

answer_2.quote: These metrics include the BLEU (-4) ngram overlap metric and BERTScore (Zhang et al., 2020), a model-based metric for measuring semantic similarity between generated inferences and references.

answer_4.quote: For human evaluation, we assess generated inferences using the same pool of qualified workers who annotated the original data.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators assessed overall quality on a 1-5 Likert scale (coherence and relevance without copying), indicated if implications made headlines more or less trustworthy, rated viewpoint (majority or minority), and indicated social acceptability.
